goal: Adds the core BIP352 (Silent Payments) cryptographic logic as a standalone module in src/common, wrapping the new secp256k1 silentpayments API.
Lets wallets, RPCs, and node code later build silent-payments sending and receiving without needing full transaction/wallet machinery to test the crypto.
Part of a long-tracked project (issue #28536) to bring a privacy-improving payment scheme into Bitcoin Core.
reviewability: Ready: author just pushed a reduced-scope version addressing the API-design feedback from the last review round.
No material open request is unanswered; the scope-narrowing (dropping CTxDestination integration) was itself the outcome of consensus discussion.
agreement: Strong: multiple concept ACKs (w0xlt, rkrux, josibake) and no NACKs across four months of deep review.
Extensive substantive design discussion converged on a cleaner API (theStack, josibake, rustaceanrob), with the author adopting the suggested direction and reducing scope accordingly.
No standing unresolved objection; remaining comments are nits and iterative refinements the author is actively addressing.

result.summary: This PR adds a new src/common/bip352.{h,cpp} module implementing the core BIP352 Silent Payments cryptography (output/tweak generation, scanning, labels) by wrapping the new libsecp256k1 silentpayments module, plus BIP test-vector unit tests, a new bech32 'sp' HRP and chain-param entries, and a small KeyPair helper. It is the second iteration of a previous attempt (#28122) and depends on the not-yet-merged secp256k1 silentpayments module (bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1765). After extensive review the author narrowed scope, removing an earlier attempt to plug Silent Payments into CTxDestination/key_io, deferring that integration decision to the consuming (sending) PR.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core currently has no way to send or receive BIP352 Silent Payments, a privacy-improving payment protocol that avoids on-chain address reuse; users and wallet implementers who want this privacy feature have been waiting since the project was opened as issue #28536. This PR supplies the foundational, wallet-independent cryptographic building blocks so that sending/receiving PRs (e.g. #35302) and other consumers can be built and reviewed against a stable core API.

open_concerns: Whether the final public API shape (SilentPaymentsReceiver, label handling, error types) is fully settled; several structural revisions occurred through the review (rustaceanrob and josibake proposed alternative APIs that the author partly adopted).
Whether crypto edge cases (invalid outputs, empty key sets, unknown witness versions) are all handled without possible crashes; several such issues were raised by w0xlt and fixed.
resolved_concerns: Multiple secp256k1 API misuse and crash-risk bugs found by theStack, w0xlt, and josibake were fixed by the author in subsequent pushes (invalid pubkey handling, index preservation bug, unknown segwit version skip, empty key set guard).

Disagreement over whether Silent Payments addresses should be a CTxDestination was resolved by removing that integration from this PR and deferring the decision to the sending PR, per consensus among josibake, rustaceanrob, and the author.
Naming, doc, and micro-style nits were addressed across many force-pushes.

categories.rationale: P4 because the only kernel-library touch is adding a chain-specific bech32 HRP string and a getter, with no effect on the kernel API surface, ABI, or any external kernel consumer; it is incidental to the real change.

categories.rationale: P2 because this is a new cryptographic primitive module whose correctness matters node-wide once consumed (theStack and w0xlt found and fixed several crash/parsing hazards during review), and it is explicitly the dependency that unblocks the sending PR (#35302) and the whole Silent Payments project (#28536) that users have long awaited for improved privacy.

The PR depends on an unmerged upstream secp256k1 PR (bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1765) for final merge, which is outside this repo's PR numbering and thus not captured in dependencies.depends_on.
result.card: This PR implements the core BIP352 Silent Payments cryptography as a new src/common/bip352 module, wrapping the not-yet-merged libsecp256k1 silentpayments API, together with BIP test-vector unit tests and small supporting changes (bech32 'sp' HRP, chainparams field, a KeyPair accessor). It solves the lack of any Silent Payments building blocks in Bitcoin Core, a privacy feature tracked since issue #28536, and is a direct prerequisite for the sending PR (#35302) and further wallet/RPC integration. Four months of deep, substantive review (theStack, w0xlt, josibake, rustaceanrob) found and fixed multiple crash/correctness hazards and converged on a cleaner receiver-centric API; the author just reduced the PR's scope (2026-09-16) to defer the still-open question of how Silent Payments addresses should integrate with CTxDestination to a later PR. Agreement is Strong, with concept ACKs and no unresolved objections. It depends on the companion secp256k1 module PR merging upstream before this can itself be merged.'
